en.title: Alaska Senate race investigated for alleged voter confusion scheme
en.dek: The U.S. Department of Justice has opened an investigation into a fake candidate in Alaska's Senate race, while Democratic lawmakers who endorsed Mary Peltola have not condemned the alleged scheme.
facts: DOJ alleges voter fraud by fake candidate in Alaska Senate race
Democratic lawmakers who endorsed Mary Peltola have not condemned the alleged scheme
DOJ approved a $3 billion Patriot missile sale to Ukraine
Federal judge blocked DOJ threats against election workers ahead of 2026 midterms
Judge ordered the administration to stop the threats
body: According to Die Zeit, the U.S. Department of Justice has alleged voter fraud by a fake candidate in Alaska's Senate race. The allegation centers on a candidate who is not a registered voter.
Fox News reported that Democratic lawmakers who endorsed Mary Peltola stayed silent when asked to denounce the alleged scheme. The lawmakers have not issued a statement regarding the investigation.
The DOJ's investigation follows a broader scrutiny of election integrity in the United States. The agency cited irregularities in voter registration records.

Earlier this week, a federal judge blocked the Trump administration from threatening election workers with prosecution over ballots tied to suspected noncitizens. The judge ordered the administration to cease the threats.
The judge's order was issued ahead of the 2026 midterm elections, according to The Hill. The order aims to prevent intimidation of election officials.
In a separate matter, the U.S. Department of Defense approved a $3 billion sale of Patriot missiles to Ukraine, according to Dawn. ABC Australia reported the same valuation.
The sale was confirmed by Congress, as reported by Dawn. The approval is part of a broader effort to support Ukraine's defense capabilities.
en.context: The DOJ has investigated alleged voter fraud in multiple states during the 2026 election cycle, according to Die Zeit. A federal judge recently blocked the Trump administration from threatening election workers, as reported by Fox News and The Hill. The U.S. approved a $3 billion Patriot missile sale to Ukraine, reported by Dawn and ABC Australia.

en.dek: A federal judge halted DOJ threats against election workers, while Congress approved a $3 billion Patriot missile sale to Ukraine.

The judge ordered the administration to stop the threats, according to The Hill. The order aimed to prevent intimidation of election officials, the outlet noted.
The Trump administration approved a potential sale of Patriot missiles to Ukraine, according to Dawn. The approval was part of a broader effort to support Ukraine's defense capabilities.
ABC Australia reported that the sale was valued at $3 billion, according to the Australian broadcaster. The figure matches the amount approved by Congress, the source said.
Congress approved the sale of Patriot missiles to Ukraine, according to Dawn. The approval was confirmed by the U.S. Congress, the outlet reported.

The DOJ had threatened election workers with prosecution over ballots tied to suspected noncitizens, according to Fox News. The threat was linked to claims that noncitizens were involved in voting, the outlet said.

The order came ahead of the 2026 midterm elections, the judge's decision was aimed at preventing intimidation of election officials, Fox News reported. The decision was seen as a safeguard for election integrity, the outlet added.

de.dek: Ein Bundesrichter stoppte die Drohungen des DOJ gegen Wahlhelfer, während der Kongress einen Patriot-Missil-Verkauf in Höhe von 3 Milliarden US-Dollar an die Ukraine genehmigte.
body: Ein Bundesrichter verhinderte, dass die Trump-Administration Wahlhelfer mit Strafverfolgung bedrohte, weil Stimmzettel angeblich mit nichtbürgerlichen Personen verbunden waren, laut Fox News. Der Richterbeschluss wurde vor den 2026 Zwischenwahlen erlassen, berichtete The Hill.
Der Richter ordnete der Administration an, die Drohungen zu stoppen, so The Hill. Der Beschluss zielte darauf ab, Wahlbeamte zu entkräften, so die Ausgabe.

Die Trump-Administration genehmigte einen potenziellen Verkauf von Patriot-Missilen an die Ukraine, laut Dawn. Die Genehmigung war Teil einer umfassenderen Anstrengung, die Verteidigungsfähigkeiten der Ukraine zu unterstützen.
ABC Australia berichtete, dass der Verkauf 3 Milliarden US-Dollar wert war, laut dem australischen Sender. Die Summe entspricht dem vom Kongress genehmigten Betrag, so die Quelle.
Der Kongress genehmigte den Verkauf von Patriot-Missilen an die Ukraine, laut Dawn. Die Genehmigung wurde vom US-Kongress bestätigt, berichtete die Ausgabe.

Das DOJ hatte Wahlhelfer mit Strafverfolgung wegen Stimmzetteln bedroht, die angeblich mit nichtbürgerlichen Personen verbunden waren, laut Fox News. Die Drohung war mit Behauptungen verbunden, dass Nichtbürger am Wählen beteiligt waren, so die Ausgabe.
Der Beschluss kam vor den 2026 Zwischenwahlen, der Richter beschloss, Wahlbeamte zu entkräften, Fox News berichtete. Die Entscheidung wurde als Schutz der Wahlintegrität gesehen, so die Ausgabe.

Das Justizministerium hatte Wahlhelfer wegen Strafverfolgung bedroht, weil Stimmzettel mit vermuteten Nichtbürgern in Verbindung standen, so Fox News.
